A 53-year-old male teacher presents for his annual physical examination in June, four weeks before his
planned month-long trip to Taiwan. His medical history includes allergic rhinitis and hypertension,
managed with fluticasone and lisinopril. Though born in Taiwan, he immigrated to the United States as
an infant and completed all recommended childhood vaccinations through high school. His current
vaccination status includes annual influenza shots, complete COVID-19 vaccination series, and a
tetanus-diphtheria (Td) booster administered 5 years ago. He currently smokes half a pack of
cigarettes daily and drinks alcohol occasionally. Which of the following vaccines should be
administered at this visit? Answer Choices: (A) Pneumococcal vaccine (B) Tdap booster (C) Shingles
vaccine (D) Hepatitis A vaccine (E) Meningococcal vaccine (F) Typhoid vaccine (G) Japanese
encephalitis vaccine (H) MMR booster (I) Hepatitis B vaccine (J) Yellow fever vaccine
 A. Yellow fever vaccine
B. MMR booster
C. Japanese encephalitis vaccine
D. Typhoid vaccine

E. Hepatitis B vaccine
F. Pneumococcal vaccine
G. Meningococcal vaccine
H. Tdap booster
I. Shingles vaccine
J. Hepatitis A vaccine
